title: hotfix: slo-enforcer regional failover + load-shedding stability
author: Evan R. Goldman
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer during regional failover and reduce over-shedding. Addresses incidents where aggressive backoff + concurrent regional failover caused cascading load-shedding and SLO violations.
description:
Summary:

This hotfix improves the SLO enforcer's backoff and decision logic to avoid excessive load-shedding during regional failover events. In recent incidents (see SUP-1198 / ENG-4872) we observed that simultaneous circuit-breaker tripping across regions led to aggressive global backoff, causing client requests to be dropped even when downstream capacity in other tiers was available.

Root cause:

- The SLO enforcer used a single global backoff token bucket per customer across all regions. During a regional failover, multiple regions would mark the same customer as degraded and trigger concurrent backoff increments.
- The ordering of decrement and recovery signals was racy under high churn, allowing the enforcer to overshoot and stay in an over-shed state for minutes.
- Load-shedding thresholds did not consider graceful fallback routes (e.g., route to compatible model variant or lower-tier capacity).

Changes in this PR:

- Introduce region-scoped backoff buckets with a coordinated, non-blocking reconciliation step to prevent double-counting recovery signals.
- Add a short-lived "grace window" (5s) where recovered capacity in any region prevents escalation of global shed state.
- Prefer fallback routing to compatible model variants before shedding client traffic. A new decision path consults routing policy and available capacity pools.
- Reduce default backoff multiplier for transient failures from 2.0 -> 1.25 and cap exponential backoff at 30s for enforcer-triggered sheds.
- Add observability: per-region backoff metrics (slo_enforcer.backoff.{region}), shed_reason tags, and a new alert rule for >10% unexpected sheds in 1m.

Testing and validation:

- Unit tests for region-scoped bucket reconciliation and race conditions.
- Integrated canary in perf-canary cluster validating normal traffic, simulated region outage, and failback. Canary run: 10k ops/s for 30m with injected region drop; verified no >5% extra sheds post-failover.
- Manual chaos test: coordinating two region controllers to trigger a staggered failover; confirmed no global overshoot.

Rollout plan:

- Deploy hotfix to staging, run canary for 1h.
- Gradual rollout to region us-east-1 (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with metrics gating on shed rate and P95 latency.
- If shed rate increases >3x baseline or SLO violations observed, automatic rollback to previous enforcer version.

Rollback:

- Revert PR via previous canary tag; enforcer configuration keys are feature-flagged under feature.slo_enforcer.regional_backoff. Disabling the flag restores prior behavior immediately.

Related notes and references:

- Incident runbook: SUP-1198 (internal link).
- Design doc: ENG-4872/backoff-regional-design.md.

Checklist:

- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration canary results attached
- [x] Observability dashboards updated
- [x] Rollout/rollback plan documented
